nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart county, IN
EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EDT TUESDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

FXUS63 KIWX 161806
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
106 PM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- While some shallow fog is possible late tonight into early
  Tuesday morning, widespread dense fog is not anticipated at
  this time. 

- A moderating temperature trend this week. The warmest days are 
  Thursday through Saturday with highs in the low to mid 60s.

- Mainly dry conditions are expected this week with some rain
  chances returning Saturday night into Sunday morning.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 105 PM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

High pressure will edge east over the next several days. With 
the slow transition, this will lead to modest temperatures
increases each day and possibly some lingering overnight/early
morning fog/stratus issues. Xover temps will be met tonight as
we head towards freezing once again and stagnant flow remains.
Considered adding patchy fog, but soundings suggest it may be
much more shallow and isolated in nature for many areas. As a
result, left it out and deferred to evening shift to monitor 
trends.

A long wave trough, preparing to approach southern CA, will come
onshore and eventually move NE into the Dakotas by 00Z Thu and 
the U.P of MI by 00Z Fri. The overall upper flow will remain
southwesterly across the region, with a push of warmer air into
the area. Highs will climb into the 60s for Thu-Sat. The area
will remain dry being removed from the best moisture and lift
well to the NW. 

While the aformentioned trough heads NE, another upper low 
settles in further north, centering on Oregon by 6Z Fri. This 
feature will eventually eject towards the region to bring what 
may be the only chance for precip over the next 7 days. Timing 
looks to be Saturday evening into Sunday morning, but overall 
rainfall amounts likely will be on the lower side. In the wake 
of this front, a return to more seasonable temps occurs Sunday 
and then well below normal (low to mid 40s) by Monday.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 105 PM EST Mon Nov 16 2026

VFR conditions should dominate most, if not all, of the period
as high pressure remains in control. Some concerns that shallow
fog could re-develop later tonight, but confidence in coverage 
and impacts at either airport is low at this time. 

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Fisher
AVIATION...Fisher

spc.text:
SPC AC 161947

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0147 PM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

   Valid 162000Z - 171200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected through tonight.

   ...20Z Update...
   No changes were made with this update. The deeper convection and
   related lightning potential has generally remained off the Pacific
   Northwest Coast, where a north/south-oriented stationary boundary
   and several embedded MCVs are present. Some of this activity may
   move onshore later today as the upper trough and accompanying
   surface boundary shift inland, though thunderstorm coverage should
   remain isolated. See the previous discussion below for more
   information.

   ..Weinman.. 11/16/2026

   .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1002 AM CST Mon Nov 16 2026/

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough off the CA Coast this morning will gradually amplify
   as it moves inland, approaching the Great Basin and Southwest by
   early Tuesday morning. Cold temperatures aloft, with 500 mb
   temperatures around -25 to -30 C, may support occasional lightning
   flashes with low-topped convection across the coastal Pacific
   Northwest and northern/central CA today. As large-scale ascent
   associated with the upper trough spreads eastward and lapse rates
   diurnally steepen, isolated thunderstorms could develop into parts
   of the Great Basin and lower CO River Valley late this afternoon
   into tonight. Overall, modest low-level moisture and related weak
   instability are expected to greatly limit severe potential.

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0100Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 161710

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1110 AM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

   Valid 171200Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are unlikely Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Thunderstorms are expected across portions of the Florida Peninsula
   and the greater Four Corners region tomorrow through tomorrow
   evening. Latest water-vapor imagery depicts an upper wave and
   attendant convection moving across the central and northern Gulf.
   This wave will migrate eastward towards the FL peninsula through
   tomorrow as it de-amplifies. Seasonal moisture in place across
   southern FL may support a few deeper/stronger cells, but with
   stronger forcing for ascent displaced over the Gulf, the expectation
   is that the most intense convection will remain off the southwest
   coast. This activity may impact the westernmost Keys, but poor lapse
   rates with eastward extent should modulate overall storm intensity.
   Further north, modest moisture return along Florida's Atlantic coast
   may support a few thunderstorms by late Tuesday afternoon, but this
   activity should remain below severe limits. 

   Across the West, an upper wave approaching CA will continue eastward
   over the next 48 hours, overspreading the Four Corners during peak
   heating Tuesday afternoon. Despite strong mid-level flow, buoyancy
   profiles are expected to remain too shallow and modest to support
   deep/robust convection. 12z guidance suggests gusty winds may
   accompany the stronger cells, but convective wind gusts should be
   comparable to background pressure gradient-driven gusts within the
   higher terrain.

   ..Moore.. 11/16/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 161917

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0117 PM CST Mon Nov 16 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Cool and stable conditions will preclude thunderstorm activity for
   much of the country on Wednesday. An upper wave currently moving
   into the northern Gulf will stall to the west of the FL peninsula
   through mid-week. South/southwesterly flow within the warm advection
   branch of the cyclone will promote northward moisture flux along the
   peninsula and support scattered to widespread showers and
   thunderstorms through the day. Weakening mid-level winds through the
   period will limit deep-layer shear and the potential for organized
   convection. 

   Across the Plains, a surface low will intensify in tandem with the
   passage of an upper wave. Very modest moisture return ahead of a
   tightening surface trough/dryline, coupled with cool mid-level
   temperatures aloft, may support adequate buoyancy for shallow
   convection. While confidence in thunderstorm potential is limited,
   the QPF signal along the surface boundary was sufficient to maintain
   thunder probabilities (refined to where guidance depicts the
   greatest overlap of buoyancy and an appreciable QPF signal).

   Along the West Coast, an upper wave will begin impinging on the
   OR/northern CA coast early Wednesday morning. Cold temperatures
   aloft will likely support isolated to scattered thunderstorms along
   and just off the coast - especially within plume of higher theta-e
   air that is forecast to move onto the northern CA coast through
   mid-day. Strongly sheared wind profiles may support a few stronger
   cells off the coast, but it is unclear whether these storms will
   maintain intensity as they move onshore where surface-based buoyancy
   should diminish precipitously.

   ..Moore.. 11/16/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS03 PTSDY3 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0830Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
